questions.prompt: A {q}-oz box costs ${p}. What is the unit price per ounce?
questions.explanation: ${p} ÷ {q} oz = ${ANSWER} per ounce.

questions.prompt: Option A: {qa} oz for ${pa}. Option B: {qb} oz for ${pb}. What is the LOWER unit price, in cents per ounce?
questions.explanation: A: ${pa} ÷ {qa} oz; B: ${pb} ÷ {qb} oz. The lower one is {ANSWER} cents per ounce, that option is the better value.
questions.hint: Divide price by ounces for each.

questions.prompt: A ${p} jacket is {a}% off, then an extra {b}% off at checkout. Final price?
questions.explanation: ${p} × (1 − {a}%) × (1 − {b}%) = ${ANSWER}. Stacked discounts multiply; they don't add.

questions.prompt: Stacked discounts of {a}% and {b}% equal what single discount (%)?
questions.explanation: 1 − (1 − {a}%)(1 − {b}%) = {ANSWER:pct}, less than {a} + {b}.

questions.prompt: Price ${p} with 6% sales tax and a ${c} coupon applied BEFORE tax. Total?
An item 'originally $200, now $99!' sells for $105 everywhere else and was never actually sold at $200. The real discount is about…
questions.explanation: Compare to the real market price ($105): (105 − 99)/105 ≈ 6%. Inflated 'original' prices are a common trick.

questions.prompt: 'Buy 2, get the 3rd free' on ${p} items. Effective discount per item if you buy 3 (%)?
questions.explanation: You pay for 2 of 3: each costs 2/3 of the price → {ANSWER:pct} off.

questions.prompt: A ${m}/month gym membership vs. ${d} per visit. How many visits per month make the membership cheaper? (Smallest whole number of visits)
questions.explanation: Break-even = ${m} ÷ ${d}; more than that and the membership wins: {ANSWER:int} visits.

questions.prompt: Your monthly take-home pay is ${N}. Using the 50/30/20 rule, how much a month goes to WANTS?
Net pay ${N}. Needs total ${e}. What percent of pay goes to needs?
questions.explanation: ${e} ÷ ${N} = {ANSWER:pct}. Over 50% means wants or savings must shrink.

questions.prompt: Find the error: Income $3,000. Rent $1,200, food $400, transport $150, fun $600, savings $500, debt minimum $250. Total planned?
questions.explanation: 1,200 + 400 + 150 + 600 + 500 + 250 = 3,100. The plan spends $100 more than income, cut fun or savings.

questions.prompt: A zero-based budget means…
choices: Every dollar of income is assigned a job
You spend nothing at all that month
You budget as if income were zero
questions.explanation: Every dollar is assigned to something (including savings).

questions.prompt: Irregular expenses: car insurance ${a}/year, gifts ${b}/year, car registration ${c}/year. How much should you set aside per month?
questions.explanation: (${a} + ${b} + ${c}) ÷ 12 = ${ANSWER} per month, so annual bills don't wreck one month.

questions.prompt: Your fixed costs are ${f}/month and your income ${i}/month. If you lose your job, how many months does a ${s} emergency fund last?
questions.explanation: ${s} ÷ ${f} = {ANSWER} months.

questions.prompt: Saving {r}% of a ${N} monthly net pay, how many months to build a 3-month emergency fund if expenses are ${e}/month?
questions.explanation: Goal = 3 × ${e}; monthly saving = {r}% × ${N}; months = {ANSWER:int}.

questions.prompt: $1 = £{r}. Convert ${d} to pounds.
questions.explanation: ${d} × {r} = £{ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: £1 = ${r}. A £{p} train ticket costs how many dollars?
questions.explanation: £{p} × {r} = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: A booth charges a {c}% commission plus gives $1 = £{r}. How many pounds for ${d}?
The dollar strengthens against the pound (more pounds per dollar). For an American visiting London, things feel…
questions.explanation: Each dollar buys more pounds, so London prices cost fewer dollars.

questions.prompt: A weaker pound makes British goods cheaper abroad. Who benefits most?
questions.explanation: Foreign buyers can afford more British goods, boosting exporters' sales.

questions.prompt: Buy rate $1 = £{b}, sell-back rate £1 = ${s}. Change $500 to pounds and immediately back. Dollars you end with?
questions.explanation: $500 × {b} × {s} = ${ANSWER}. The difference from $500 is the booth's spread.

questions.prompt: Using a card abroad, you're asked 'Pay in USD or GBP?' Choosing your home currency (USD) often…
choices: Adds the merchant’s poor exchange rate
Saves money by skipping bank fees
Is required by UK law for tourists
Is always free on any card
questions.explanation: Dynamic currency conversion usually uses a worse rate. Paying in the local currency is often cheaper.

questions.prompt: Rent ${r}/month rises 3% per year. Rent in year 2?
Total rent paid over 5 years: ${r}/month, rising 3% each year.
Buying a ${H} home: 3% closing costs to buy and 6% to sell later. Combined transaction costs?
questions.explanation: 9% × ${H} = ${ANSWER} (ignoring price changes).

questions.prompt: Price-to-rent ratio = home price ÷ annual rent. A ${H} home rents for ${r}/month. Ratio?
questions.explanation: ${H} ÷ (12 × ${r}) = {ANSWER}. Above ~20 often favors renting; below ~15 favors buying.

questions.prompt: Which costs does a homeowner pay that a renter usually doesn't?
choices: Property tax, upkeep and home insurance
The monthly phone and internet bill
Bus and train fares to work
questions.explanation: Owners pay these 'hidden' costs on top of the mortgage.

questions.prompt: Opportunity cost of a big down payment is…
choices: The return that money could have earned
The interest charged on the mortgage
The purchase price of the home itself
The yearly property tax on the home
questions.explanation: Money tied up in a down payment can't be invested elsewhere, that forgone return is a real cost of buying.

questions.prompt: Annual maintenance is roughly 1% of home value. On a ${H} home, about how much per month?
questions.explanation: 1% × ${H} ÷ 12 = ${ANSWER} per month.

questions.prompt: Renter's insurance is ${r}/month. Homeowner's insurance on a similar home is ${h}/month. Annual difference?
A ${b} restaurant bill, plus a {t}% tip on the bill. You pay with ${p}. Change due?
questions.explanation: Bill plus tip: ${b} × (1 + {t}%), rounded to the cent. ${p} minus that = ${ANSWER}.
questions.hint: Work out the tip and add it before making change.

questions.prompt: Minimum number of coins & bills ($20, $10, $5, $1, 25¢, 10¢, 5¢, 1¢) to make ${c}?
questions.explanation: Use the largest denomination first (greedy), {ANSWER:int} pieces.

questions.prompt: Split a ${b} dinner bill evenly among {n} friends, adding an {t}% tip on the pre-tax total. Each pays?
questions.explanation: ${b} × (1 + {t}%) ÷ {n} = ${ANSWER} each.

questions.prompt: You have $300 left after needs. Concert ($150), emergency fund (currently $200), and new sneakers ($120). Best order of priorities?
choices: Emergency fund first, then one want
Concert and sneakers now, fund later
Put all three on a credit card
questions.explanation: With only $200 of cushion, building the emergency fund protects you; then choose a want that fits.

questions.prompt: Cash-back card: {c}% back on ${s} of monthly groceries. Yearly cash back?
questions.explanation: 12 × ${s} × {c}% = ${ANSWER}, only worth it if you pay the balance in full.

questions.prompt: A 0%-interest 'buy now, pay later' plan for a $400 phone has a $35 late fee per missed payment. The biggest risk is…
choices: Overspending, then fees on missed payments
There is no risk with 0% interest
questions.explanation: BNPL makes purchases feel smaller; missed payments add fees and can hurt credit.

questions.prompt: A ${p} laptop: extended warranty costs ${w}. If there's a {r}% chance you'd need a ${f} repair, what is the expected repair cost?
questions.explanation: {r}% × ${f} = ${ANSWER}. If that's well below the warranty price, the warranty is usually a bad deal.

questions.prompt: Cutting a ${d}/day takeout habit to ${n}/day saves how much per year (365 days)?
Price elasticity: if a 10% price increase drops quantity sold by 25%, demand is…
questions.explanation: % change in quantity (25%) > % change in price (10%) → elastic.

questions.prompt: Price elasticity = %Δquantity ÷ %Δprice. Price rises {p}%, quantity falls {q}%. Elasticity (as a positive number)?
questions.explanation: {q} ÷ {p} = {ANSWER}. Above 1 = elastic.

questions.prompt: Which good likely has the most INELASTIC demand?
questions.explanation: People need medicine regardless of price; brands of soda are easily substituted.

questions.prompt: Your budget keeps failing because 'small' purchases add up. The best fix is…
choices: Track a month of spending and set limits
Stop budgeting, it clearly doesn’t work
Put everything on credit cards instead
Ignore purchases under $10 from now on
questions.explanation: Tracking reveals leaks; category limits make them visible before they grow.

questions.prompt: Unit price: {n} batteries for ${p}. Price per battery?
questions.explanation: ${p} ÷ {n} = ${ANSWER} each.

questions.prompt: Equity after {y} years: home bought for ${H} grows {g}%/yr; mortgage balance remaining is ${B}. Equity?
questions.explanation: Value = ${H} × (1 + {g}%)^{y}; minus ${B} owed = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: Which is a VARIABLE expense?
questions.explanation: Variable expenses change month to month; fixed ones stay the same.

questions.prompt: Pay-yourself-first means…
choices: Saving only what is left over
questions.explanation: Automatic saving at payday makes saving the default instead of the leftover.

questions.prompt: Membership warehouse: ${m}/year fee; it saves you {s}% on ${g}/month of groceries. Net yearly savings?
Inflation of {i}%/yr. How much will a ${p} basket of groceries cost in {y} years?
Which is the strongest reason to buy store brand over name brand?
choices: Same quality at a lower unit price
The packaging is plainer and simpler
Name brands cost more to recycle
questions.explanation: Compare ingredients and unit price; store brands often match name brands for less.

questions.prompt: Monthly net pay ${N}; you save ${s}. Savings rate (%)?
questions.explanation: ${s} ÷ ${N} = {ANSWER:pct}.

questions.prompt: A security deposit on a rental is…
choices: Money held for damage, usually returned
Your first month’s rent paid early
A city tax on every rental lease
A fee the landlord keeps no matter what
questions.explanation: Leave the place in good shape to get your deposit back.

questions.prompt: A ${p} item is marked up {m}% and then put on a {d}% sale. Final price?
questions.explanation: ${p} × (1 + {m}%) × (1 − {d}%) = ${ANSWER}, a 'sale' after a markup can still cost more than the original.
